claims.text: For \(i=j=1\), \(a=\min(q-1,r-1)\), \(b=1\), and \(N=\binom{a+1}{a}=\min(r,q)\); the two displayed families specialize to \(\{h_1,\ldots,h_{\min(r,q)}\}\) and \(\{e_1,\ldots,e_{\min(r,q)}\}\).

If \(a=0\), equivalently \(i=q\) or \(j=r\) under \(1\le i\le q,\ 1\le j\le r\), then \(N=1\); both proposed families are the singleton \(\{s_{i^j}\}\). These are trivial minimality cases provided \(s_{i^j}\ne0\) and Theorem 5.4’s generation assertion is used.
The smallest interior case with \(b>1\) is \((r,q,i,j)=(3,3,2,2)\), where \(a=1\), \(b=2\), \(N=3\), and the two families are \((22,32,33)\) and \((22,221,222)\).

The prior finite certificate for \((r,q,i,j)=(5,6,2,2)\) gives \(N=10\), quotient \(\mathbb Z^{10}\), and basis candidates \(F_1=(22,32,33,42,43,52,44,53,54,55)\) and \(F_2=(22,221,2211,222,22111,2221,22211,2222,22221,22222)\); it supports the conjecture conditionally on the Pieri presentation and generation hypotheses.
